facts.statement: The genus Pervushovisaurus was described by Arkhangelsky in 1998.
facts.quote: authority: Arkhangelsky, 1998

facts.statement: Pervushovisaurus lived during the Upper Cretaceous (Cenomanian) in the Saratov region of western Russia.
facts.quote: Pervushovisaurus is a genus of platypterygiine ichthyosaur from the Upper Cretaceous (Cenomanian) Melovatka Formation in the Saratov region in western Russia

facts.statement: Fossils of Pervushovisaurus have been found in the La Penthiève Beds of France and the Cambridge area of the United Kingdom.
facts.quote: the La Penthiève Beds of France and the Cambridge area of the United Kingdom

facts.statement: Pervushovisaurus was originally classified as a subgenus of Platypterygius but was later elevated to full generic rank due to distinct features.
facts.quote: It was originally described as a subgenus of Platypterygius, but later work showed that it was sufficiently distinct from the type species of Platypterygius, P. platydactylus, to be elevated to full generic rank.

facts.statement: Pervushovisaurus was a medium-sized ichthyosaur that measured 5.8 meters in length.
facts.quote: Pervushovisaurus was a medium-sized ichthyosaur measuring 5.8 m long.

facts.statement: Pervushovisaurus is characterized by foramina along the ventral premaxillary-maxillary suture, a semi-oval foramen on the premaxilla, lateral ridges on the maxilla, and a wide supranarial wing on the nasal bone.
facts.quote: presence of foramina along the ventral premaxillary–maxillary suture; presence of a semi-oval foramen on the lateral surface of the premaxilla, anteroventral to the external naris; presence of lateral ridges on the maxilla; presence of wide supranarial 'wing' of the nasal

facts.statement: The mandible of Pervushovisaurus features a robust splenial protruding from the external surface and a root with a quadrangular cross-section where cementum forms prominent 90-degree angles.
facts.quote: robust splenial markedly protruding from the external surface of the mandible; root with quadrangular cross-section, with the cementum forming prominent 90° angles.

facts.statement: Pervushovisaurus possesses a secondarily closed naris surrounded by foramina.
facts.quote: secondarily closed naris surrounded by foramina

facts.statement: Pervushovisaurus has an elongated anterior process of the maxilla that reaches the level of the nasal bone.
facts.quote: elongated anterior process of the maxilla, reaching anteriorly the level of the nasal

facts.statement: The rostrum of Pervushovisaurus is straight.
facts.quote: rostrum straight

facts.statement: Pervushovisaurus had straight, non-recurved tooth crowns.
facts.quote: straight, non-recurved tooth crowns

facts.statement: Pervushovisaurus belongs to the family Ophthalmosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Ophthalmosauridae

facts.statement: Pervushovisaurus is classified within the subfamily Platypterygiinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Platypterygiinae

facts.statement: Pervushovisaurus lived during the Upper Cretaceous (Cenomanian stage), approximately 100 to 94 million years ago.
facts.quote: que vivió durante el Cretácico Superior (etapa del Cenomaniense, hace 100-94 millones de años)

facts.statement: Pervushovisaurus inhabited the Saratov Oblast in western Russia.
facts.quote: en el óblast de Saratov en el occidente de Rusia

facts.statement: The type species P. bannovkensis is known exclusively from the partial skull holotype SGU 104a/24.
facts.quote: La especie tipo de Pervushovisaurus, P. bannovkensis, es conocida exclusivamente a partir del fósil holotipo SGU 104a/24, un cráneo parcial.

facts.statement: A specimen of P. campylodon found in the La Penthiève Beds of France was described in 1882 by Henri Émile Sauvage.
facts.quote: A specimen of P. campylodon was found in the La Penthiève Beds of France and was described in 1882 by Henri Émile Sauvage.

facts.statement: In 2016, the species P. campylodon was referred to Pervushovisaurus, having previously been allied with Ichthyosaurus since 1846.
facts.quote: In 2016, an additional species of Platypterygius from England and France, P. campylodon, was also referred to Pervushovisaurus after previously being allied with Ichthyosaurus in 1846.

facts.statement: The time range for Pervushovisaurus extends from the Albian to the Cenomanian, between 113.2 and 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Cenomanian (113.2 to 93.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are 14 recorded fossil occurrences of Pervushovisaurus.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 14
